topic: Historical Background and Making of Indian Polity
description: The Indian Constitution evolved through a series of acts passed during British rule. It was drafted by the Constituent Assembly, formed in 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan, establishing the supreme law of independent India.

sections.title: Company Rule (1773-1858)
sections.description: Early legislative acts passed by the British Parliament to control and regulate the affairs of the British East India Company in India.

historical_events.significance: Designated the Governor of Bengal as the 'Governor-General of Bengal' (Lord Warren Hastings was the first); led to the establishment of the Supreme Court at Calcutta in 1774.
Separated the commercial and political functions of the Company; created a new body called the 'Board of Control' to manage political affairs.
Made the Governor-General of Bengal the 'Governor-General of India' (Lord William Bentinck was the first). It was the final step towards centralization in British India.

important_facts.fact: The Charter Act of 1853 introduced an open competition system for the selection and recruitment of civil servants (Macaulay Committee was appointed in 1854).

sections.title: The Crown Rule (1858-1947)
sections.description: Following the Sepoy Mutiny of 1857, the British Crown assumed direct control over the administration of India.

historical_events.significance: Changed the designation of the Governor-General of India to 'Viceroy of India' (Lord Canning was the first). Created a new office, 'Secretary of State for India'.
Introduced a system of communal representation for Muslims by accepting the concept of a 'separate electorate'. Lord Minto came to be known as the Father of Communal Electorate.
Introduced 'Dyarchy' (dual rule) in the provinces and 'Bicameralism' (two houses) with direct elections at the center.
Proposed the establishment of an All-India Federation; introduced 'Provincial Autonomy' in provinces and 'Dyarchy' at the center.

important_facts.fact: The Government of India Act of 1935 is the largest and most significant structural source of the present-day Indian Constitution.

sections.title: Formation of the Constituent Assembly
sections.description: The historical process of demanding and eventually establishing the Constituent Assembly to draft the Constitution of India.

historical_events.significance: The idea of a Constituent Assembly for India was put forward for the first time by M. N. Roy, a pioneer of the communist movement in India.
The British Government, for the first time, accepted the demand for a Constituent Assembly in principle.
The Constituent Assembly was officially constituted under the scheme formulated by the Cabinet Mission Plan.

important_facts.fact: The total strength of the Constituent Assembly was originally 389 (296 seats allotted to British India and 93 to the Princely States).
The first meeting of the Assembly was held on December 9, 1946, where Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was elected as the temporary President.
On December 11, 1946, Dr. Rajendra Prasad and H.C. Mukherjee were elected as the permanent President and Vice-President of the Assembly, respectively.

sections.title: Major Committees of the Constituent Assembly
sections.description: To handle different tasks of constitution-making, the Assembly appointed several committees. Here are the most important ones and their chairpersons.

key_associations.extra_info: Set up on August 29, 1947, consisting of 7 members. It was the most important committee, tasked with preparing the draft of the new Constitution.
Dealt with defining the powers of the central government.
Dealt with the integration of princely states and provincial matters.
Oversaw the general proceedings and functioning of the Constituent Assembly.

key_concepts.explanation: Moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on December 13, 1946. It laid down the fundamentals and philosophy of the constitutional structure and eventually took the form of the Preamble.

sections.title: Enactment and Enforcement of the Constitution
sections.description: The final stages of completing, adopting, and legally enforcing the Constitution of India.

historical_events.significance: The people of India 'adopted, enacted, and gave to themselves' the Constitution. Provisions related to citizenship, elections, and provisional parliament came into force immediately.
Members signed the Constitution; the National Anthem (Jana Gana Mana) and National Song (Vande Mataram) were officially adopted.
The Constitution came into full force. This date was chosen as Republic Day to commemorate the 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) resolution passed in 1930.

important_facts.fact: It took the Constituent Assembly exactly 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to finalize the Constitution.
The original Constitution of 1950 contained a Preamble, 395 Articles (divided into 22 Parts), and 8 Schedules.
Sir B. N. Rau was appointed as the Constitutional Advisor (Legal Advisor) to the Constituent Assembly.
